observations: (a) The first full run's failure on criterion 2 was one existing test, TrueMobbing.test_a_member_added_mid_card_joins_the_mob_at_once_and_stays_in_the_rotation, which seated a Claude member (ctx-9) beside four models with quota. Changing it in the green was the right call: the test is about a member added mid-card voting at once and joining the next rotation, the Claude seat was incidental to that point, and refusing exactly that roster is what criterion 2 requires, so the failure was the new gate working on an old fixture. Moving the member to Codex and asserting the second Codex vote keeps the test's point; making the fake probes show Claude as the only model with quota would have changed the fixture's world for no gain, and an exemption in the gate would have defeated the criterion. Claude-seat starts stay covered where they belong, in tests/test_quota_first.py (every other model down). What was not right: the break was found by a 20-minute run, not by the red, and the change is explained only in the green's body; the reviewer should confirm it with one mutation (break the mid-card join and see the test fail).

(b) The same green rewrote a guard: PureRules.test_claude_own_probe_is_never_a_reason_to_refuse now passes 'claude' inside expected, because the Claude-filter mutation stayed green with the old list; the green's body shows the mutation failing it (failures=1). The slice's rule (a guard whose mutation does not turn it red is rewritten) worked a second time.
(c) Plain failover turns are not gated for quota (no fixed backend before they run), as the red said; the slice's Not-in list does not name it, so the reviewer should state it as a known limit.
